name: Dasiglucagon
route: Single-dose injection under the skin (autoinjector or prefilled syringe)
status: FDA-approved in 2021 for severe low blood sugar in people with diabetes aged 6 and older
mechanism: A stabilized copy of glucagon that tells the liver to release stored glucose, rapidly raising dangerously low blood sugar

article.summary: Dasiglucagon (Zegalogue) is a ready-to-use glucagon analog in an autoinjector, FDA-approved since 2021 to rescue severe low blood sugar in people with diabetes aged 6 and up.
article.takeaway: Dasiglucagon is a modified form of glucagon, the hormone that tells the liver to release sugar. Unlike older glucagon kits, it stays stable as a liquid, so there is nothing to mix in an emergency. In its pivotal adult trial, blood sugar began recovering a **median of 10 minutes** after the shot, compared with 40 minutes on placebo.[^1] Nausea and vomiting are the main side effects, and anyone given a rescue dose still needs emergency help and food once they can swallow.[^2]
glance: Severe hypoglycemia in people with diabetes aged 6 and older
One 0.6 mg injection under the skin, given by a caregiver or bystander
Three placebo-controlled phase 3 rescue trials in adults and children

blocks.text: Glucagon is made by the pancreas and acts as the counterweight to insulin. When blood sugar drops, it signals the liver to break down its glycogen stores and release glucose into the blood. In people who use insulin, an overdose or missed meal can push sugar so low that they become confused, pass out or have a seizure, and cannot eat their way out of it.

Natural glucagon clumps into fibers when dissolved, which is why traditional kits ship as a powder to be mixed at the scene. Dasiglucagon is a 29-amino-acid analog with a handful of amino acid swaps that keep it stable in water. It works on the same glucagon receptor, but comes ready to inject.

Zegalogue is approved to treat severe hypoglycemia (dangerously low blood sugar) in children 6 and older and adults with diabetes.[^2] It is meant for situations where the person cannot safely take sugar by mouth, and it is usually kept at home, school or work for family members, teachers or coworkers to use.
Each phase 3 trial lowered blood sugar with insulin under medical supervision, then gave a single dose and timed how long glucose took to climb by at least 20 mg/dL.

rows: 10 minutes vs 40 on placebo; 12 with standard glucagon[^1]

blocks.text: In the adult trial, 99% of people given dasiglucagon recovered within 15 minutes, a rate similar to reconstituted glucagon.[^1]

The dose for adults and children 6 and older is 0.6 mg, injected under the skin of the lower belly, buttocks, thigh or outer upper arm. The label says to call for emergency help right after giving it, to give a second dose from a new device if there is no response after 15 minutes, and to offer carbohydrates by mouth once the person can swallow.[^2]
Devices are stored in the refrigerator but can be kept at room temperature for up to 12 months, which makes them easier to carry.[^2]

items: **Common:** nausea, vomiting, headache, diarrhea and pain at the injection site
**Allergic reactions** can occur, as with other glucagon products
**Not for:** people with pheochromocytoma (an adrenal tumor, where it can spike blood pressure) or insulinoma (where it can trigger a rebound low)
**May not work** when the liver has little stored glycogen, such as during starvation, adrenal insufficiency or long-standing low blood sugar; glucose is used instead

blocks.text: Zegalogue was approved in March 2021 and is marketed in the US by Novo Nordisk. Developer Zealand Pharma has also tested dasiglucagon as a continuous pump infusion for congenital hyperinsulinism, a rare condition in which babies overproduce insulin. In a randomized trial in 32 children, adding it to standard care did not reduce finger-stick lows, but continuous glucose monitors recorded 43% fewer low readings in a later analysis.[^5]

The FDA turned back that application twice, in late 2023 and October 2024, over inspection problems at a contract manufacturing plant rather than the clinical data.[^6] As of 2026 the congenital hyperinsulinism use remains unapproved.

evidence.label: Approved: consistent placebo-controlled rescue trials
evidence.text: Three randomized, double-blind phase 3 trials in adults and children showed fast, reliable recovery from induced low blood sugar.[^1][^3][^4] These trials were done in controlled clinical settings, not in real emergencies, which is standard for rescue drugs.

faq.q: How is dasiglucagon different from regular glucagon?
faq.a: Both raise blood sugar the same way. Dasiglucagon comes as a ready-to-use liquid, while traditional [glucagon](/peptides/glucagon) kits must be mixed first; newer glucagon options also include a premixed pen and a nasal powder.
In clinical testing, blood sugar started to recover a median of about 10 minutes after the injection.[^1][^3]
It is designed so that a trained family member, friend or coworker can give it. Emergency services should still be called right away.
